topic: Someone finds their childhood teddy bear at a yard sale
text: I shouldn't be surprised, but I am, to find this old teddy bear at a yard sale. The worn, threadbare fur, the button eyes staring into some forgotten past—how many years have passed? The bear feels lighter than I remember, maybe the stuffing has settled, or maybe I've just grown. I trace the stitches, fraying at the seams, thinking about the childhood it cradled. I wonder who owned it, if they knew the comfort it brought, the silent keeper of secrets. I hesitate, my hand hovering above it, almost afraid to claim it, to take it home where it might just sit, another relic of time, another forgotten friend.
